title: Iro AI vs Coursiv: which AI learning app is right for you in 2026?
metaTitle: Iro AI vs Coursiv: Reviews, Pricing and Which to Pick
lede: Both teach you to use AI in a few minutes a day. The real difference is how you learn, and how you pay.
keyTakeaways: Iro AI and Coursiv both teach AI in short daily lessons but differ in teaching style and pricing.
Iro AI is practice-first: drills, duels, and instant feedback rather than passive video lessons.
Coursiv sells auto-renewing 1-, 4- and 12-week plans and shows the price only at checkout; Iro AI is $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year with a free tier.
Coursiv rates 4.6 on Trustpilot from about 143,000 reviews; the complaints that do appear are mostly about extra charges and refunds.
Pick Iro AI if you learn by doing; pick a course app if you prefer guided video lessons.

fit.forWho: People who want to get good at using ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other AI tools by practicing for about five minutes a day, rather than following a guided lesson.
fit.fixes: Knowing AI exists but getting generic or wrong answers from it. You write real prompts, fix weak outputs and spot made-up facts, with feedback each time.
fit.notFit: you want a sit-back guided course, you need an accredited certificate, or you are on Android and want a native app (Iro is iOS plus a web app for now).

description: Iro AI vs Coursiv in 2026: Coursiv reviews and pricing from its own pages, App Store and Trustpilot, how the two apps teach, and who each one suits.

sections.heading: What does Coursiv do well?
sections.html:
Coursiv is a mobile-first AI learning app that walks beginners through tools like ChatGPT and image generators using short daily lessons, often packaged as a 28-day challenge. It has reached a large audience and reviewers generally praise the clean design, clear instructions, and the low-pressure, bite-sized pace.

If what you want is a guided curriculum (open the app, watch and read today's lesson, tick it off) that structure is genuinely helpful, especially when you're starting from zero and want someone to tell you what to learn next.

sections.heading: What do Coursiv reviews and pricing say in 2026?
sections.html:
Pricing. Coursiv's own pricing page lists no dollar amounts. It says Coursiv is a subscription with 1-week, 4-week and 12-week plans that renew automatically, and that the exact price, including any trial or intro price, is shown on the checkout screen before you pay. On the US App Store, Coursiv's in-app purchases appear as "Coursiv Premium" at $9.99, $29.99 and $79.99, without the plan lengths. Its subscription terms say a trial converts to a paid plan unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends, and that Coursiv may change its fees with reasonable notice.

Refunds. Coursiv's refund policy, last updated October 18, 2026, offers a full refund within 14 days of purchase only if you haven't used the product yet, and usually for the first payment only. Coursiv says it may decline other requests unless the law requires a refund. If you paid through Apple, the refund request goes to Apple. Our Coursiv cancellation guide walks through each route.

Reviews. On Trustpilot, Coursiv shows a TrustScore of 4.6 from about 143,000 reviews, with 67% five-star and 2% one-star, and it replies to every negative review. Positive reviews mostly say the lessons are clear and easy to follow for beginners. Critical ones say the content can feel basic or close to what is free online, and some describe refund requests that were turned down. On the App Store, some reviewers say an extra offer during sign-up charged them on top of the plan they picked, and one says a refund depended on finishing coursework. Coursiv's replies say add-on offers are optional and prices are shown before purchase.

The upshot: most reviewers are happy with the lessons, and the complaints cluster around billing. Before you pay, note the plan length and renewal price on the checkout screen, skip add-ons you didn't come for, and set a reminder before any trial ends.

Prices, ratings and policies come from Coursiv's pricing and legal pages, its App Store listings and its Trustpilot page, read on November 21, 2026. Reviews are what reviewers report, not claims we verified.

sections.heading: How is Iro AI different from Coursiv?
sections.html:
Iro AI starts from a different belief: you don't learn a skill by watching it, you learn it by doing it. So instead of a video course, Iro is built like a game: short, interactive drills where you answer, get instant feedback, build streaks, and climb rank tiers as the skill sticks.

The lessons are organized into dedicated paths for the tools people actually use, a ChatGPT path, a Claude path, a Gemini path, and more. And before you commit to anything, you can take the free AI IQ test to see where you stand. New to all this? Start with the 30-day AI plan for beginners.

The scale is worth stating plainly, because a drill-based app can sound slighter than a video course when it is the opposite. Iro is 34 paths, 522 lessons and 3,000+ exercises across 23 exercise types. The Prompt Lab sends prompts you write to a live model and grades them, Ask Iro explains what you got wrong by chat or voice, and duels, Custom Paths, an Image Lab and claimable certificates sit alongside. Every path is open on the free tier, paced by a battery that gives you a full lesson a day.

sections.heading: How much do Iro AI and Coursiv cost?
sections.html:
This is where the two apps differ most, and it's worth being clear-eyed about.

Coursiv sells auto-renewing 1-week, 4-week and 12-week plans and shows the exact price, including any intro offer, only at checkout. Auto-renewal and add-on charges are the most common things critical reviewers say caught them off guard, so read the checkout screen before you pay. The reviews and pricing section above has the details.

Iro AI keeps it simple: Pro is $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year (about $4.17 a month) with a 7-day free trial, you can cancel anytime in your Apple settings, and the free tier opens every path at a pace of a full lesson a day.

Third-party prices and ratings here are US figures at the time of writing and change without notice. Last reviewed November 21, 2026.

sections.heading: Should you choose Iro AI or Coursiv?
sections.html:
A simple way to decide:

  • You learn best by doing, want to actually retain the skill, and like simple, predictable pricing? Iro AI.
  • You prefer a sit-back, guided course with a daily lesson to watch and don't mind a recurring subscription? Coursiv is a fair pick.

Honestly, the best move costs nothing: take the free AI IQ test first. It shows you exactly which AI skills you're missing, and that tells you what to learn next, in whichever app you choose. If you want to compare the underlying tools too, see ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini.

faq.q: Is Iro AI a good Coursiv alternative?
faq.a: Yes, especially if you learn by doing. Coursiv is built around guided lessons in a 28-day challenge, while Iro AI is built around active practice (short interactive drills with instant feedback) plus a free tier and simple pricing: $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year.

faq.q: How much does Coursiv cost vs Iro AI?
faq.a: Coursiv sells auto-renewing 1-week, 4-week and 12-week plans and shows the exact price at checkout; its US App Store in-app purchases are listed at $9.99, $29.99 and $79.99. Iro AI Pro is $9.99 a month or $49.99 a year (about $4.17 a month) with a 7-day free trial, and you can start free.

On Trustpilot, Coursiv has a 4.6 TrustScore from about 143,000 reviews, and most reviewers say the lessons are clear and beginner-friendly. Critical reviews, there and on the App Store, mostly mention content that feels basic, add-on charges at sign-up, and refund requests that were turned down.

Coursiv's refund policy offers a full refund within 14 days of purchase if you haven't used the product, usually for the first payment only. App Store purchases are refunded through Apple. See our Coursiv cancellation guide.

faq.q: Does Coursiv have a free trial?
faq.a: Coursiv's terms describe a trial, sometimes paid, that turns into a paid plan unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends. Any trial or intro price is shown at checkout. Iro AI has a free tier plus a 7-day free trial of Pro.

faq.q: Which app actually helps you retain AI skills?
faq.a: Retention comes from practice and recall, not just watching. That's why Iro AI is built on quizzes, drills, and feedback loops rather than video lessons. See why active practice beats passive learning in our 30-day plan.

faq.q: Is there a free Coursiv-style way to learn AI?
faq.a: Yes, unlike Coursiv, Iro AI is free to start. You can build real skill without paying first. Here are the best free ways to learn AI, and a wider comparison of AI learning apps if you want to weigh the options.
